lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hey Barbara, Ana here. How's your Wednesday going?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What happened with the cooking at home?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good! I didn't miss a day.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You figured that out on your own.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the cooking at home going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it. I don't want to end up like my dad.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your body is still recovering, and pushing it feels risky right now.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the cooking at home going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everything at the store costs so much. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, work has been crazy, I'm doing overtime.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're giving everything to work right now, and there's not much left over for you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You feel like you have to do something.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've always eaten late, that's how we do it at home.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've tried before and it didn't stick.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Work has been crazy, I'm doing overtime.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, work makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you cook on Sundays?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. I don't know where the day goes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd do it if the day had a few more hours.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My diabetes is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your family is a big part of why.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need this for my head too, not just my body.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If finding the time gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll go to the mall instead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 4 out of 4 days, the hard part was finding the time, and next week you're going to cook at home 5 nights. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Barbara. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

flags.reason: Participant says everything at the store costs so much; possible food-access/cost barrier was not explored before moving on.
Coach repeats the exact open question from line 6 without engaging the intervening barrier talk, which reads as scripted.

score.summary: Ana used frequent reflections and affirmations, and built a concrete plan with a backup for time barriers. However, she repeated an earlier question verbatim and did not explore the cost barrier raised at line 18.
strengths: Line 8 and line 36 use complex reflections that capture Barbara's ambivalence well.
Line 19 affirms the starting step, and line 35 respects her knowledge of her schedule.
Line 48 plans for barriers with a backup plan, and line 50 summarizes the plan before closing.
coaching_tips: At line 17, avoid repeating the line 6 question; reflect the barrier she just named instead.
After line 18 (store costs, uneven days), ask a brief open question about food affordability before moving on.
Consider asking permission before suggesting steps, as at line 33, to keep Barbara in control of the plan.
